findings.mechanism: R1 connects /IN (pin 1) to /OUT (pin 2) per work/netlist/design.xml. With /OUT clamped to 0 V, the full 48 V appears across the 10 kOhm resistor in steady state; C1 (100n, /OUT to GND) carries zero DC current and cannot relieve it. Dissipation P = V^2/R = 48^2/10000 = 0.2304 W at I = 4.8 mA, sustained indefinitely. This exceeds the stated 0.1 W continuous limit by a factor of 2.30 (margin +0.1304 W). An ngspice-42 DC operating-point simulation with the clamp modeled as an ideal external 0 V source confirms v(out)=0, I(R1)=4.8 mA, P(R1)=0.2304 W. Even if R1 were +10% high (11k), dissipation is 0.209 W, still over 2x the limit, so the conclusion is not tolerance-sensitive.
findings.reasoning: This is the single criterion the exercise asks to evaluate, and the design fails it by a wide, tolerance-insensitive margin under a condition explicitly stated to persist indefinitely. The passing ERC/DRC results (work/erc/erc.json, work/drc/drc.json) are connectivity/rule checks and carry no information about dissipation, so they do not contradict this finding. Hand calculation and an independent ngspice operating-point simulation agree exactly at 0.2304 W versus the 0.1 W continuous limit, making this an evidence-supported blocking defect rather than a concern.
findings.title: R1 dissipates 0.23 W continuously, 2.3x its 0.1 W limit, under the stated 48 V clamp condition

limitations: Resistor self-heating/derating not modeled; the 0.1 W figure was treated as a hard continuous limit exactly as stated in the exercise assumption
R1 tolerance and part model are not specified in the design; nominal 10k was used (noted in experiments that even +10% resistance leaves dissipation >2x the limit)
